reports.summary: E-library is finished. I made the predecessor's half-done edits coherent: the committed tree builds, and its broken E-07 test, which could never drive SwiftUI keyboard focus in an offscreen window, is replaced by tests that read the accessibility tree. I then worked through the whole list. New fixes: the compact header now fits the 216 pt column of a 480 pt window (crumbs fold, then the count, then Open Full Library); file-name rows truncate in the middle, as Finder does; the S40 fixture now matches Figma (Shows / Films / Anime folders, three playlists); the mini-player hover transport sits where Figma puts it (it was 1.5 pt off); breadcrumb separators use Figma's 8 pt box. New tests: view-level tests for E-07, E-10, E-11, the import-notice row and the minimum width; model tests for the mixed-import notice; a queue-row Add to Playlist test; and a native test that runs the real -playlistMedia:complete: against a scripted media library. I made each test fail by breaking its fix on purpose, then restored the fix. Kept differences are written into DECISIONS.md: D032 (Dark styles in the Light frame), D039 (audio tracks), D042 (rows keep file names) and D044 (Home's sixth section, counts, narrow panel, audit dispositions). The library suites (about 30, including Library*, Gallery, FigmaDeviation and QueueAddToPlaylist) pass on the shared checkout. The native test passes when compiled by hand with the harness flags; I did not run tools/native-tests.py.

Each was confirmed to fail with its fix broken.

(f) LIVE Light tint: the compact library backdrop is MXRBackdropSurface(tint: bgB1Transparent), so H-design's material change (D053) reaches it with no library edit.

(c) Native playlist-complete stub: NativeLibraryPlaylistOrderRegression.m now also runs the real -playlistMedia:complete: and page against scripted vlc_ml_get / vlc_ml_list (13 assertions). With the comparison forced to YES it fails 3 assertions. Built and run by hand with the harness flags.

reports.notesForOthers: A-window: with a right panel open, the compact library gets 32% of the window (153 pt at 480 pt). That is below LibraryGeometry.compactMinimumWidth (208 pt, the narrowest header that fits), so the panel runs past its column. Please clamp compactWidth to max(LibraryGeometry.compactMinimumWidth, share*width), or hide the compact library when the panel opens on a narrow window. Without a panel, 480 pt already fits (216 pt is at least 208 pt). Integrator: tools/native-tests.py headless-regressions should be re-run (NativeLibraryPlaylistOrderRegression.m gained an engine-listing section). I-build: nothing new to wire, since the test file already exists. J-media-io / C-bridge: if the owner schedules COMP-08, the work is an audio-mode AddSubtitles matcher, ML attach with VLC_ML_FILE_TYPE_SOUNDTRACK (MXRLibraryServices attachSubtitle can take a type argument), and soundtrack slaves in MXRServicesBridge LibrarySubtitleURLs. The test build briefly failed in another agent's Tests/MXRUISnapshotTests/DialogKeyLoopControlTests.swift (MainActor isolation errors); it compiled again a few minutes later.

issues.description: Figma Player - Light 2425:13624 also draws the breadcrumb '▶' separators (I2425:13646;6131:13620/13475) with Dark/FG/A4 (#404040) and the '…' slot with Dark/FG/A2. The product draws the separators in Light fgA4 (#9A9A9A, measured 154,154,154 against Figma 64,64,64). This follows the same Dark-style slip principle, but the amendment only names the divider, rows and current crumb. One more clause would cover it. The divider kept at Light/Divider/Dim is well supported: the same Light frame uses Light/Divider/Dim twice and Dark/Divider/Dim only for this one divider.

The y of the mini transport is computed as video.height * 104 / videoBlock.width * homeCard.width / homeCard.height. That uses the home card's 316×177.75 ratio as a stand-in for the 16:9 video (375×210.94). The value is right (it works out to h*104/210.94), but the dependency on an unrelated token is hard to read. A token or constant for the video's height would be clearer.

At the 480 pt minimum window the header fits as claimed: ← → … ⋯, with sort/view/search on the second row and nothing past 216 pt; the mutation test confirms this. The cost is that rows give only ~40 pt to the label ('Th…p4'), and the current folder name is folded away. It is usable only through hover tooltips. It is documented in D044 (narrow compact panel) and is an edge case, but the owner may want a larger compact share or minimum at that size (A-window's MXRAppView.compactWidth).

E-07 checks that the static columns() matches the column count read from the drawn grid through AX, and that model moveSelection with arrowOffset selects the card drawn below. It does not drive the onKeyPress handler itself, because offscreen SwiftUI focus cannot be driven, so a broken key binding would still pass. The real keys are in liveChecks (E-arrow-keys).

These rows are still disabled while Figma shows them enabled. The amendment admits this is missing work across J-media-io and C-bridge, not an engine limit. Critic P2 explicitly allowed 'record a DECISIONS entry (out of scope …) or schedule'. So this is acceptable as an owner scheduling decision, not an excuse, but it remains a visible Figma difference until it is scheduled.

verdict.summary: Independent verification of E-library, round 1: PASS. The build is green. The targeted suites pass: Library*, LibraryViewBehaviour 5/5, LibraryImportNotice 2/2, QueueAddToPlaylist, FigmaDeviation, LibraryInteraction and LibraryModel, 86 tests across 3 targets. `tools/native-tests.py --suite headless-regressions` passes under the lock, including library-playlist-order with 13 assertions. Mutation checks in an isolated copy (../build/evidence/final4/E-library-verify-r1/pkg): with opensFull forced to `compact`, testCompactPanelDrawsInsideTheMinimumColumn fails (controls at 224 > 216.5 pt); with the compact list keyed by offset, testRowStateFollowsItsEntryWhenRowsAboveGoAway fails. So the new regression tests are real. Renders and checks are in ../build/evidence/final4/E-library-verify-r1/checks and renders, and I looked at each one. S40 Home now matches Figma 1106:5633 almost pixel for pixel (Shows/Films/Anime, three playlists, ← enabled) through a gallery-only fixture; product ranking is unchanged (figmaHomeFolderIDs is nil by default). S29 'Mark as Watched' uses the two-tone check. S46 collapsed/queue PASS and hover leaves a 1 px edge, with the fixture name matching Figma and the artist chip covered by D044. S28 narrow folds crumbs to '… ▸ S01' with middle-truncated file names. S28 minimum draws inside 216 pt. Neighbouring S28/S33/S38/S43/S44/S45 checks are identical to the fixer's after-reports, so there are no regressions. Decisions checked against figma_file.json: D042 is correct (Figma rows show raw file names). The D032 amendment is justified: in Player - Light the library divider is the one use of Dark/Divider/Dim, while Light/Divider/Dim is used twice in the same frame, and the rows/crumb Dark/FG/A2 values are unreadable on light. The D039 amendment is honest and is allowed as an owner scheduling decision under critic P2. The compact backdrop uses MXRBackdropSurface(tint: bgB1Transparent), so H-design's material reaches it. The engine is untouched (diff against upstream-base is empty). No new Swift 6 warnings appear in library sources. No new figmaDeviations were added; one, S40, was removed. Ownership was respected: only the DECISIONS amendments and two new test files are outside the owned paths. Remaining issues are minor only: undocumented Light separator colours, the minimum-width row legibility trade-off, the E-07 key-binding test not driving onKeyPress, an indirect mini-transport formula, and the pre-existing S33 'My Songs' tone.
